liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Big Boss Man** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the opener low-key and mild-mannered; Reviewer had not heard this song in a while [10][12]
- **Row Jimmy** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it pleasant but forgettable, fading from memory soon after it ends; Reviewer calls it smoking, with Jerry playing hard [10][12]
- **Gimme Some Lovin'** (2 reviews): Phil sings a line about kicking ass the way everybody should; Reviewer singles out the Gimme Some Lovin' and Phil's playing in it [13][16]
- **It's All Over Now** (1 review): Intensity builds steadily as the song develops, though it never becomes overpowering [10]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Jerry ramps up the intensity and the vocals are especially strong [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-08-13.142090.fob.oade.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.jacobs.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 153 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1987-08-13.163642.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 149 min [2]
- **gd1987-08-13.nak100.pasternak.81988.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 145 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd1987-08-13.nakcm304.beckham.suraci.82098.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 143 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this copy may not be the best quality but is far cleaner than an old, static-laden copy [16]
- **gd87-08-13.sbd.larson.21348.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 143 min; rated 4.12/5 by 17 [8]. Said about its sound: Sound is unlike other recordings the reviewer has heard, especially in the second set; the stream has bad breaks [14]

## Around the show

- Third night of the Red Rocks run; heavy rain fell until about showtime [11]
- Fans were buzzing about the upcoming Telluride weekend, unaware Bill Graham had arranged plenty of tickets [11]
- Fans worried about getting into Telluride could instead catch a Neil Young show at the Rocks that weekend [11]
- Phil laughs while singing, and the band seems relaxed and energetic [12]
- Reviewer sat fourth row and took photos during the first set; the day was rainy [15]
- Kurt Littlewing was found unconscious in a campground on 08/12/1987, which the reviewer links to the band's mood [17]
- This run came just before the Telluride 'Harmonic Convergance' weekend [21]
- This was the final Grateful Dead concert at Red Rocks [4]
- Reviewer finds the first half sloppy and slow, with the second half much stronger [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-08-13.142090.fob.oade.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.jacobs.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Blake Jacobs; source: Source Info: Oade's Master (FOB) Audience PCM; Schoeps CMC3/MK41 mics > Oade M118 > Oade modified Sony PCM-F1; Transfer Info: Master Oade PCM > Sek'd Prodif >… [1]
- **gd1987-08-13.163642.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME80 mics > Sony D5M [2]
- **gd1987-08-13.nak100.pasternak.81988.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jon Pasternak; source: Nakamichi CM-100's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Marantz 420 cassette deck, with Dolby On [4]. Also: A tape flip in Space at 4:36 was mended, with fades and cleanup done in Soundforge [4]
- **gd1987-08-13.nakcm304.beckham.suraci.82098.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Don Beckham - Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nak CM304's>Sony D5M [5]
- **gd87-08-13.sbd.larson.21348.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD:?>D>CD via Chris Larson [8]
